title: Verifier-Assisted versus LLM-Only Pre-deployment Network-Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether adding a deterministic pre-deployment validator plus a bounded automated-repair budget increases the fraction of intent-driven network-change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. Each paired intent produced one shared_initial candidate and was evaluated in two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and the restricted repair budget the single-shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We release a complete preregistration, execution, and analysis artifact bundle to support reproducibility and interpretation.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. For pre-deployment changes, semantic correctness properties—ordering/sequence constraints, reachability, and policy preservation—are operationally critical and generally not guaranteed by syntactic checks alone. A widespread engineering pattern is generate→validate→repair, where a deterministic validator enforces semantic invariants and a bounded repair operator attempts constrained corrections. Prior work documents both the promise and caveats of tool-augmented LLM workflows for NetOps and emphasizes that observed benefits depend on validator expressiveness, generator variance, and allowed repair budgets [1]–[4].  

This study asks a tightly scoped operational question: when a single LLM candidate per intent is produced (a shared_initial draw), does adding a deterministic pre-deployment validator plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that that same candidate passes semantic validation compared with accepting it without repair? Conditioning on a single draw corresponds to operational policies that restrict model calls for cost, latency, or governance reasons. We preregistered a paired confirmatory experiment that isolates deterministic rescue (no resampling per condition) and executed it with full artifact archiving. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating bounded deterministic rescue under the shared_initial estimand; (2) a complete archived execution and analysis bundle; and (3) an evidence-grounded interpretation of ceiling effects, validator coverage, and repair-budget tradeoffs for NetOps CI/CD policies.
sections.related_work: LLM applications to network management and intent-driven configuration have progressed rapidly, including systems that synthesize templates, translate intents, and generate protocol test cases [4],[6],[7]. Tool-augmented agentic frameworks—planner-centric and ReAct-style pipelines—enable LLMs to call external validators, simulators, or synthesizers and coordinate multi-step NetOps workflows [2]. Empirical and system reports show that introducing deterministic checks and generate→validate→repair scaffolds often improves surface correctness metrics relative to unconstrained generation, but reported gains depend strongly on validator coverage, task distribution, and whether pipelines permit resampling or verifier-guided regeneration [1],[3]. Research on hallucination detection and deterministic safety nets highlights complementary detection and mitigation approaches (entropy/semantic detectors, retrieval augmentation, self-reflection) that reduce false positives but whose effectiveness is task- and validator-dependent [5]. Our experiment situates itself within these threads by measuring the bounded deterministic effect of validation+single-repair on the identical LLM output rather than conflating rescue with resampling or guided regeneration [2],[3].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the confirmatory design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) and fixed the primary estimand as the absolute paired difference in the proportion of unflagged validator passes (guarded − baseline) on N = 300 paired intents after prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The preregistration and analysis executor were frozen prior to the main run. The optional pilot for discordance estimation described in the preregistration was not executed; this omission and its implications are reported explicitly below.  

Task suite and stratification. Tasks were generated deterministically into a synthetic topology suite stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high) with 100 pairs sampled per stratum. Each task manifest encodes: natural-language intent, initial and expected final device state, required_sequence constraints (ordering such as must_be_down_for_fields), preserve_unspecified_state invariants, and protected_interfaces. Difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) determined stratum assignment. Representative difficulty patterns include 'shutdown_configure_restore' (medium) and 'paired_link_atomic_mtu_change' (hard).  

Shared_initial protocol, models, validator, and repair. To isolate deterministic rescue from generator resampling benefits we used a shared_initial protocol: for each pair the pipeline produced exactly one LLM candidate which was reused verbatim for both baseline and guarded conditions. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic validator implementing a full_intent_constraint_validation rule that checks sequencing invariants, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability invariants encoded by the synthetic suite, and forbidden-template protections for protected interfaces. The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair attempt (repair budget ≤ 1); the repair operator was a constrained localized edit routine limited to sequencing and local insertion edits. Repair attempts were applied only if the validator flagged the shared_initial candidate and were re-validated deterministically. Binary scoring (unflagged vs. flagged) defined success for the estimand.  

Execution, auditing, and stopping rules. The run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter in scientific_confirmatory mode. The preregistered stopping rule required halting if >20% of attempted pairs were excluded due to dual-call outages; no such condition occurred. The run adhered to the prespecified model-call budget. All provider/audit counters, stage counts, and per-episode validator traces were archived in the run bundle.  

Analysis procedures. The preregistered confirmatory analysis used a paired binary executor that reports the contingency counts (n11, n10, n01, n00), computes the absolute paired difference, applies an exact two-sided McNemar test, and constructs a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI. The archived bootstrap parameters were seed = 1729 and resamples B = 10000. Secondary and stratum-wise tests were treated as exploratory and subject to multiplicity control where reported. Sensitivity analyses (failure-as-zero, stratified tests) were preregistered and archived as exploratory outputs.  

Reproducibility and artifact availability. A complete artifact bundle (preregistration, task manifests, model configuration, validator traces, repair traces, execution logs, and analysis inputs) was archived to permit deterministic replay of the confirmatory executor. Interested readers can consult the archived run bundle (manifest included in archive) for full low-level logs and traces.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The adapter completed the confirmatory run yielding complete_pair_count = 300 under the shared_initial protocol; model-call usage was low (one shared_initial generation per pair plus one repair invocation observed in the run). Deterministic reconciliation confirmed consistent episode accounting and absence of dual-call outages.  

Primary outcomes. Binary scoring returned baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The exact two-sided McNemar test on the observed discordant counts (n10,n01) produced p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. Minimal discordance (m = n10 + n01 = 1) limits inferential sensitivity in this sample and bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point in this experimental context.  

Per-stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per-stratum tallies were: low baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100 and guarded = 100/100. The single discordant pair occurred in the high stratum. For that episode the validator flagged a sequencing-invariant omission (a missing 'admin down' before a VLAN/MTU change); the constrained single repair performed a localized insertion of the missing sequencing step and the validator reported valid == true after the edit, producing the deterministic rescue observed. The repair was the only repair invocation in the confirmatory run.  

Contamination and missingness. Preplanned contamination checks and negative controls did not indicate unexpected passes; no pairs were excluded under preregistered rules and no provider/infrastructure dual-call outages occurred.  

Operational cost. The guarded pipeline produced one deterministic rescue at the cost of one additional repair-stage invocation across 300 pairs, indicating minimal marginal model-call expenditure for bounded deterministic rescue under this synthetic suite and repair operator design.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting the null discordance. The observed near-ceiling baseline (299/300) reduces the room for bounded deterministic rescue under the shared_initial estimand. Because the preregistered pilot for discordance estimation was not executed, the main run confronted an empirical baseline that produced minimal discordance and hence limited statistical power to detect small absolute differences. This outcome highlights the practical value of small calibration pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling on a chosen task suite.  

Estimand conditioning and operational alignment. The shared_initial estimand conditions on a single LLM draw and therefore measures only deterministic validator/repair rescue applied to that draw. Workflows that permit resampling, verifier-guided regeneration, or interactive steering change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates by exploiting generator variance; evaluations of such workflows should be preregistered under the corresponding estimand. Organizations must choose evaluation estimands that match operational policies (model-call budgets, allowed automated edits, human escalation rules).  

Validator coverage and failure-mode dependence. The single observed failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes such as reachability or ACL removal were not prevalent in this synthetic suite. The marginal utility of a guarded pipeline will therefore depend on task-distribution failure-mode prevalence and on validator expressiveness. Richer validators that capture reachability and policy semantics may increase rescue opportunity; conversely, strict human-review policies that disallow automated edits limit the guarded pipeline to detection and escalation.  

Repair budget tradeoffs. We deliberately limited the permitted automated repair to one constrained edit to measure bounded deterministic rescue. Iterative repair, broader edit operators, or verifier-guided regeneration would estimate different operational tradeoffs and likely increase rescue frequency at the cost of additional model calls and governance complexity.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired confirmatory run (N = 300 paired intents) that conditioned on a single shared_initial LLM candidate per intent, adding a deterministic validator plus ≤1 automated repair produced one deterministic rescue: baseline = 299/300, guarded = 300/300, absolute paired improvement = 0.00333 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). Under the supplied synthetic suite, generator single-shot quality was near ceiling, limiting observable rescue under a bounded repair budget and the shared_initial estimand. These results illustrate the importance of matching the experimental estimand to intended operational policies (model-call budgets and permitted automated edits). We release the complete preregistration, execution, and analysis artifact bundle to enable targeted follow-up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, or repair budget to quantify tradeoffs in other deployment regimes.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated deterministically for the study; real-world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase validator marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and the declared deterministic validator were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single-shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre-specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post-preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
